title: People Ops: Hiring, Onboarding, Performance & Manager Guide
author: Sofia Martinez
content:
Overview

This document consolidates Redwood Inference's People Operations guidance for hiring, employee onboarding, our performance and feedback cycle, and explicit manager responsibilities. It is intended for hiring managers, people-ops partners, and people leaders who run interview loops, onboard new teammates, and lead performance conversations. The goal: consistent candidate experience, predictable onboarding velocity, and objective performance processes that scale as the company grows.

Table of contents
1) Hiring process overview
2) Interview loop guidelines and scorecard
3) Offer approval and compensation workflow
4) New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)
5) Performance and feedback cycle (annual + mid-year)
6) Manager guide: 1:1s, calibration, and career conversations
7) Templates and appendices

1) Hiring process overview

Short intro: Redwood uses a standardized, bias-reduced hiring process to ensure quality, fairness, and speed. People-ops partners with hiring managers to define role profiles, run effective interview loops, and track pipeline metrics.

Key principles:
- Candidate experience: transparency, timely updates (48 business hours for scheduling), and respectful communication.
- Role clarity: every requisition must have a public-facing job brief and an internal success profile (expectations at 30/60/90 days).
- Structured evaluation: interviewers use role-specific scorecards and evidence-based rubrics.
- Compliance: all offers must pass background check, eligibility verification, and legal review for restricted roles/regions.

Hiring lifecycle (high level):
1. Requisition creation: hiring manager submits req in Greenhouse with job brief and 30/60/90 success profile.
2. Sourcing & screening: TA reviews, sources candidates, and runs initial phone screen.
3. Interview loop: on-site / virtual loop using standardized rubrics.
4. Calibration and decision: interviewers submit scorecards, hiring manager convenes debrief within 48 hours.
5. Offer & approvals: compensation approval, legal review, and offer issued.
6. Acceptance & background checks: candidate accepts; people-ops initiates background and I-9 (US) / local equivalents.
7. Onboarding initiation: new-hire packet and start-date logistics coordinated by people-ops.

SLA targets:
- Time-to-fill goal: 45 days for IC roles, 60 days for senior/lead roles.
- Offer turnaround: 48 business hours from verbal approval to offer issuance.
- Interview scheduling: initial scheduling within 5 business days of phone screen.

2) Interview loop guidelines and scorecard

Interview types and ownership:
- Recruiter screen (TA): culture fit, logistics, basic skills.
- Technical screen (Engineering): coding/architecture for eng roles or relevant technical assessment.
- Deep-dive interview(s): product sense, design, behavioral, and role-specific exercises.
- Manager interview: alignment to team goals and role expectations.
- Leadership interview (senior roles): scope, influence, execution track record.

Panel size: 4-6 interviewers for IC roles, 5-8 for leadership roles. No more than one rep from the candidate's immediate team should be on the first-round panel to avoid bias.

Scorecard (required fields):
- Skill competency (1-5) with evidence examples
- Role-specific domain knowledge (1-5)
- Communication & collaboration (1-5)
- Growth mindset and coachability (1-5)
- Overall hire/no-hire recommendation (yes/maybe/no)
- Notes / evidence: concrete examples tied to rubric

Bias-mitigation rules:
- Use the job brief and 30/60/90 success profile as the rubric anchor.
- Avoid questions about protected classes; if sensitive topics arise, flag with people-ops.
- Interviewers must submit scorecards before debrief.

3) Offer approval and compensation workflow

Approval path:
1. Hiring manager determines target comp and equity recommendation in partnership with People Ops compensation lead.
2. People Ops runs market comp check and approves within budget band.
3. Finance & Legal sign-off for senior hires (>L5) or if total comp exceeds predefined thresholds.
4. People Ops issues formal offer letter and negotiates final terms.

Offer components checklist:
- Base salary, target OTE (if applicable), bonus plan, and equity (grant schedule & cliff).
- Start date and reporting manager.
- Work location and relocation policy if applicable.
- Benefits summary link and health coverage effective date.
- Contingencies: background check, employment eligibility, IP agreements.

Template: Offer approval matrix (text):
- IC L1-L3: People Ops approval required, Finance notified for exceptions.
- IC L4-L5: People Ops + Finance approval.
- L6+ / Director: People Ops + Finance + Legal approval.

4) New hire onboarding checklist (first 90 days)

Onboarding philosophy: accelerate time-to-contribution while connecting new hires to culture, peers, product, and tooling. Ownership is shared: People Ops manages logistics; hiring manager owns role enablement and ongoing ramp.

Preboarding (before day 1):
- Send welcome email with first-day agenda and required forms.
- Create accounts: Slack, email, Okta, payroll, HRIS (Workday), and access to team drive.
- Hardware procurement: laptop imaged, peripheral checklist, shipping confirmation.

Day 1-7 (orientation & setup):
- Company orientation (People Ops): benefits overview, policies, code of conduct, security baseline.
- Team welcome: meet-and-greet, 1:1 with manager scheduled twice in week 1.
- Technical setup: dev environment guide, repo access, and required credentials.

30-day goals:
- Complete product orientation and read key docs (architecture overview, API guides).
- First small deliverable assigned (bug, doc, or small feature).
- Cross-functional introductions: product, SRE, and adjacent teams.

60-day goals:
- Take ownership of a non-trivial task with mentor support.
- Present work in a team demo.
- Midpoint check-in with manager and people-ops.

90-day goals and onboarding sign-off:
- Demonstrated independent ownership of a scoped area.
- Manager completes probation checklist and confirms ongoing role expectations.
- People Ops completes administrative closeout (benefits enrollment confirmation, payroll).

Onboarding artifacts (links/attachments):
- First-90-days success profile template (copyable)
- Technical ramp plan examples by role (Engineering / Product / Support)
- Mentor pairing process and expectations

5) Performance and feedback cycle

Cadence and goals:
- Annual performance review cycle: calendar-year reviews with planning in November and formal calibration in December.
- Mid-year check-in: June review for ongoing adjustments and development goals.
- Quarterly 1:1s and quarterly goals (team-level OKRs) to drive execution.

Components of the review:
- Self-assessment: documented achievements, metrics, and examples (submitted 1 week before manager review).
- Manager assessment: competency ratings, impact, and promotion readiness commentary.
- Calibration: cross-team managers review ratings to ensure consistency and remove biases.
- Calibration panel attendees: manager, manager's manager, and HR business partner; for senior roles include director-level stakeholders.

Rating scale (example):
- Exceeds expectations
- Meets expectations
- Needs improvement

Promotion and leveling:
- Promotion readiness is based on demonstrated impact, scope, and system-level thinking. Use the published leveling rubric and provide evidence mapped to business outcomes.
- Requests for out-of-cycle promotions must include a short packet: impact summary, peer feedback, manager endorsement, and compensation request. People Ops assesses equity/budget implications.

Improvement plans:
- Performance improvement plans (PIPs) are a last resort and follow a documented process: clear objectives, measurable success criteria, dedicated coaching resources, and a 60-90 day timeline. PIP ownership is the manager with HR partner oversight.

6) Manager guide: 1:1s, calibration, and career conversations

Core manager responsibilities:
- Regular 1:1s (recommended weekly for ICs, biweekly for senior ICs) with clear agendas and notes saved in manager toolkit.
- Clear expectation-setting at hire and ongoing role check-ins (30/60/90).
- Timely feedback: deliver both positive reinforcement and corrective feedback within one week of observing behavior.
- Career development: own career ladder conversations, ID growth projects, and make stretch assignments.

1:1 best practices:
- Create recurring agenda items: priorities, blockers, career & growth, feedback.
- Use the Start/Stop/Continue format for focused action items.
- Document decisions and follow-ups in the manager toolkit (link).

Calibration & compensation conversations:
- Prepare calibration packet: manager assessment, evidence snippets (metrics, customer impact), and comp recommendations.
- Calibration meeting norms: show evidence first, avoid anchoring on past labels, and seek consensus.

Manager escalation matrix:
- People management issues: escalate to HR business partner.
- Legal or compliance incidents: escalate to Legal and Security immediately.
- Performance issues that may lead to PIP: consult People Ops before initiating.

Included templates (copy/paste):

Appendix A: Common FAQs
Q: What is the expected notice period?
A: Standard is 2 weeks for ICs; leadership roles commonly request 4 weeks. Exceptions recorded in offer letter.

Q: Who approves equity grants?
A: People Ops recommends, Finance approves for senior roles, and the CEO signs for director+ grants.
